<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 771b2db20ac08d78b7fec5c2bd1ee30de9aa26dc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3fbc14233b1bda266ab6bfd81aa844700ea4abb8` — the merge of head `0b0d0e216f41f563de1d94a86e9e985d7f673c3f` into base `771b2db20ac08d78b7fec5c2bd1ee30de9aa26dc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3fbc14233b1bda266ab6bfd81aa844700ea4abb8 && git checkout 3fbc14233b1bda266ab6bfd81aa844700ea4abb8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 771b2db20ac08d78b7fec5c2bd1ee30de9aa26dc 0b0d0e216f41f563de1d94a86e9e985d7f673c3f && git checkout -B drift-repro 771b2db20ac08d78b7fec5c2bd1ee30de9aa26dc && git merge --no-ff 0b0d0e216f41f563de1d94a86e9e985d7f673c3f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 771b2db20ac08d78b7fec5c2bd1ee30de9aa26dc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 771b2db20ac08d78b7fec5c2bd1ee30de9aa26dc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d33de915d2443d420720cf532d47ac5d7b741dfb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts, .changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md, .changeset/org-admin-removal-stored-row-verdict.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal, the gate call site, step 2.7, the query guard), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (getCallerPreImage, readRowById, callerCannotReadAddressedRow), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-name.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/organization-scope.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/CHANGELOG.md, the gate at tag @objectstack/plugin-security@18.3.0, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md (D12 and its 2026-10-17 note), scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, ruling comment 5985885287 and the rest of the #21771 thread, the #30165 thread (records 6638950952 and 6640676948), the #30200 body, the PR body, file list, net diff and the check-runs on this head.

Review order: an at-tier review on a security hardening PR (the ruling's own landing condition). Read-only: the diff against origin/main, the PR body, the cited code at this head and the check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run. Mechanism, where a judgment needed one, is in the reviewer's local security-note and nowhere in this record (security-findings.md section 6).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The organization branch now judges a by-id removal on the stored row once the caller's own read returns the row.** `organizationTargets` asks `callerRead` whether there is a row, and only then reads the stored row; `organizationAdminFailure` runs the organization, position and permission-set checks on that row. Right. ADR-0090 D12 (2026-10-17 note) defines the organization administrator's right over "every permission set the row distributes", a fact of the stored row, so judging on a read that a field rule or masking rule has thinned judges less than the row. It is also the rule the delegated branch has held all along (`delegatedTargets`). Consequence, declared in the body and the changeset: a removal of an in-boundary row whose judged column the administrator does not read at its stored value is now admitted where published 18.3.0 refused it; an out-of-boundary one stays refused. A widening of admitted writes, not of the published contract (see ②).
2. **A refusal names a value only when the caller can read it at its stored value (or wrote it).** Three new unnamed sentences (organization, position, permission set), each behind `mayName`, each with `meta: {}`; the position's carried set is named only beside a named position; the grant's column asked of `mayName` is `GRANT_SET_NAME_FIELD`, the same column `grantSetNameOf` reads. Right. `columnsReadAsStored` is strict equality against the system read, so a hidden column (absent) and a masked column (different string) are both unnamed; an object-valued column compares unequal and is left unnamed, which is the safe direction.
3. **A row the caller cannot read and an id naming no row keep the read door's not-found.** `prev` is null when `callerRead` returns null, the `unreadable` refusal is unchanged, and `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal` still maps it to `recordNotFoundError` for the addressed id. Right, and no stored read is made for such a row (the stored read is conditional on the caller's read; pinned in the unit file).
4. **Inserts unchanged.** The insert target now carries `wrote: null`, which makes `mayName` true for every column of a payload row, so every insert sentence names what it named. Right.
5. **Update unchanged.** The update refusal is taken before any lookup (#30200's order); the merge kept both docblock texts and the code path. Right.
6. **A read refusal or a store fault still propagates** from either read; the middleware answers a declared 4xx read refusal with that refusal and lets a 5xx through. Unchanged from the base.
7. **Public surface unchanged.** `DelegatedTarget` is a module-private interface; `GRANT_SET_NAME_FIELD` is an internal import; `index.ts` still re-exports `DelegatedAdminGate`, `isTenantAdmin` and the `DelegatedAdminGateDeps` type from the gate module and nothing more; no error code, no spec schema, no metadata key moves. Right.
8. **One extra system read per admitted-or-refused removal of a readable row.** A cost, not a surface change; the unit file pins that it is not issued for an unreadable row.

Disclosure rule (security-findings.md section 6) on the PR title, body, commit messages, both changesets, test names and code comments: each states the hardening rule (what the verdict is taken on, what a refusal names, what answers not-found); none describes a probe or how the pre-fix door could be made to misbehave. The ablation lines name the pins they red, not a recipe. No breach.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`; `Clause-②: no` with no arm; `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the body and on both changesets. **Right.** The brief's question, answered from the repo's rules: this change admits removals the published release refused, but Clause ② reads only the published contract surface (execution-duties.md: "条款②只指已发布契约面"; contract-review.md: the package's `exports` map, the schema, the error-code ledger), and its negative boundary places a runtime permission or security behaviour change outside Clause ② and on the human floor's security/permission class. No export, schema or error code moves, so the declaration is `no`; `no (widening)` is malformed under AGENTS.md's closed pair, and `(narrowing)` is false. The widening is declared in prose, which is where it belongs, and the compensating control the rules name for that class is this at-tier review before landing. The level follows the kind: `none` takes `patch`.
- **The corrected pending changeset** (`.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md`): the rewritten lead sentence, "now asks the administrator's own read, in its own context, whether that row is there to remove", is true of this tree. One note: the gate at tag 18.3.0 already read the row under the caller's context, so the sentence's "now" overstates the delta from the published release; what moved since 18.3.0 is the answer, which the first bullet states. Not a finding. **Should-fix (text):** the second bullet, "A row the administrator can read keeps the answer it had, including the guidance that names the organization boundary", is no longer true of this tree for a row whose judged column the administrator does not read at its stored value (the new changeset in this same PR says the opposite, correctly). The body's "Its bullets stay true" is wrong on that bullet. The file is already under this PR's deliberate correction, so the fix rides the same confirmation.
- `Check Changeset` is red on this head by the gate's own design: the foreign-changeset rule (#17712) names `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` as present on the merge base and changed by this PR, and its text classes the case as a DELIBERATE CORRECTION whose remedy is to say so on the PR and get it confirmed. The PR does. The maintainer's confirmation on record (#30165's thread, 2026-11-05T00:47Z) names #30144 and #30165 only; a confirmation for this PR's edit is still owed before a Tier S landing, with a PR comment recording the gate and the cause (SKILL.md's three conditions for carrying a by-design red).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **"Correcting a pending release note: please confirm."** Judged under ②: the sentence is true of the tree; the second bullet is not, should-fix. Confirmation for this PR owed to the maintainer.
2. **"The row's organization column ... how the write door's own row-level check treats a caller who does not read the organization column is with the seat."** Read, not pinned by me: under the walled postures the write door's own row-level re-read is asked under the caller's context with a predicate on that column, and the door's query guard refuses a caller-context read whose predicate names a column the caller cannot read, so such a caller's by-id removal is refused by the door whatever the gate decided, before and after this PR. Pre-existing, outside this PR's files, fail-closed, names nothing. The rig's choice to pin the gate's verdict under `group` and `isolated` and the door end to end under `single` is the honest shape. Escalated to the seat as the body asks; the seat decides whether a false refusal in that configuration is a finding to file. Not this PR's defect.
3. **"#30200 is merged in ... the merge conflicted in that docblock only."** Read at this head: the `organizationAdminFailure` docblock carries both texts coherently (read question first, stored-row verdict, `mayName`, then the update-order sentences), and the code keeps #30200's update refusal before any lookup. Resolved.
4. **Verification claims (85/85, 157/157, the whole suite, ablations A1 and A2, 60 derived gates).** Not reproduced here (read-only). CI at the time of this read: every finished check green except `Check Changeset` (by design, above), including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, the Dogfood Regression Gate and Test Core shards 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of 8; Test Core 4/8 still in progress. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; the record names what it read.
5. **Provenance of the rule.** The body, the new docblock lines, two new code comments and both new `describe` names cite "ruling of record 5985885287, sub-item B ('the verdict stays on the stored row')". Comment 5985885287 on #21771 is ruling letter A and carries no sub-item B and no such sentence; its only "B" is the option not taken. The stored-row and wording rule is the 2026-11-04 batch-4 item-2 maintainer ruling that the #30165 contract-review record (6638950952) names, and I found no tracker record carrying it. The citation pre-exists on main from #30165 at four sites; this PR extends it at five more. **Should-fix:** cite the record that decided the rule, and if that ruling has no written record of record, the seat writes one (as 5985885287 was written) and the code points at it. The design does not depend on the citation (①.1), so this is provenance, not a FAIL.
6. Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay login to name.
7. The `Implemented-by` branch and the adopting seat share one session id; ④ below was run by an isolated subagent of that seat, fed the inputs the brief names and not the seat's conclusions, as the independence rule requires.

### ④ Design judgment

For `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts`, against the ruling it implements (5985885287: a row the caller cannot read answers as a nonexistent id; a reader who may not write keeps 403 and sees nothing new), ADR-0090 D12 as amended 2026-10-17, and the code it cites. Tried to break it:

- **A caller who cannot read the row.** `callerRead` returns null, no stored read, the `unreadable` refusal, the middleware's not-found for the addressed id; a caller who also holds an adminScope falls to the delegated walk, which reads as the caller again, gets null and refuses the same way without a stored read. Holds, on both tables, in every posture the rig boots.
- **A missing or non-scalar id.** Refused as a filter delete before any read; an insert has no id. Holds.
- **A row that vanishes between the two reads.** The stored read returns null, the branch answers the unreadable refusal, the middleware re-asks the caller's read and maps to not-found. Holds.
- **Masked versus hidden.** Both fall outside `reads` under strict equality; neither reaches the sentence or `details`. A mask that is a fixed point of its value counts as read and may be named, which discloses nothing the caller does not already see. Holds; pinned at the gate (both administrator sets, both tables, each of the three judged columns, hidden and masked) and through the door (position and permission set under `group` and `isolated`, hidden and masked; organization under `single`).
- **The three tenancy postures.** Under the walled postures the caller's read is tenant-scoped, so another organization's row is unreadable and answers not-found; under `single` it is readable and is refused on the stored organization without naming it when the caller cannot read that column. Holds; the `single` control pins it end to end.
- **The delegated branch.** Untouched in code; `DelegatedTarget` is shared without changing its shape. Holds.
- **Refusal wording that could name a value the caller cannot read.** Every value a sentence or `details` can carry on the removal path (organization, position, the set a position carries, permission set) is behind `mayName`; the business-unit sentence is reachable only from an insert payload, which the caller wrote. Holds. A catalog fact (which sets a position carries) is named only beside a position the caller reads.
- **An extra read for a row the caller cannot read.** None: the stored read is conditional on the caller's read returning a row, and the unit file pins the absence of a system read of the addressed object for both an unreadable row and an id naming no row.
- **Explain and the write-admission preview.** `explainAccess` asks the gate only whether the caller covers the user; `canWriteObject` folds every refusal to a boolean. Neither can split by presence or by column visibility.

Findings: **no must-fix.** Should-fix: ② the second bullet of `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` is now false and should be corrected under the same confirmation; ③.5 the "sub-item B" citations name a record that does not carry that sub-item, so the rule's provenance should point at the record that decided it (and that ruling should have one). Escalated, not a finding of this PR: ③.2, the door's own refusal of a by-id removal by a caller whose field rules hide the organization column under the walled postures, which the seat should classify. Owed before a Tier S landing: the maintainer's confirmation of this PR's changeset correction, the by-design-red comment on this PR, and green on the three Test Core shards still running.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b0d0e216f41f563de1d94a86e9e985d7f673c3f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts, .changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md (the delta `d33de915d2..0b0d0e216f`, commits 0cc6f17e95 and 0b0d0e216f) + the rewritten PR body, ruling comment 6649064874 on #21771, every ruling citation left in packages/plugins/plugin-security/src and .changeset at this head, the check-runs on this head, and the earlier record on `d33de915d2` (comment 6649074186) this delta builds on.

Delta review by the same reviewer: the two findings-only commits since the PASS record on `d33de915d2`. Read-only, nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No accept-set or public-surface change.** Every hunk of the delta is inside a docblock, a line comment or a `describe` string: `columnsReadAsStored` and `mayName` docblocks, the `organizationAdminFailure`, `organizationTargets` and `delegatedTargets` docblocks, two delegated-walk comments, two `describe` names in the posture rig and one in the unit file, and three lines of one pending changeset. No executable line moves, no test assertion moves, no export, schema or error code moves. The behaviour judged on `d33de915d2` stands unchanged at this head.
- **Should-fix (provenance) closed.** Every citation of the stored-row verdict and of the naming rule in the package now names ruling of record 6649064874, which exists on #21771 as a written record (letter B, maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-11-04, written 2026-11-05T03:41Z, stated to add to 5985885287 and not replace it): the two helper docblocks, the organization branch's docblock and comment, the two delegated-walk comments, the `delegatedTargets` docblock, and the three describe names. The citations of 5985885287 are kept where they belong (the read door's not-found answer: `callerRead`, `UnreadableAddressedRowRefusal`, `organizationTargets`'s first paragraph, `delegatedTargets`'s first paragraph, the middleware's `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal`, the rig's not-found describes). No "sub-item B" remains anywhere in the package or in `.changeset`. The ruling record's text matches what the code does: the verdict on the stored row in both branches once the caller's own read returns the row; a value named only when the caller reads that column at its stored value; the unreadable row and the missing id unchanged.
- **The `delegatedTargets` docblock's last sentence** now says the guidance "names only what the caller may be told (`mayName`)" where it said the row "keeps its verdict and its guidance". True of the code since #30165; a comment correction, no behaviour.

§6 (`security-findings.md`) on the new public text: both commit messages, the rewritten body (the new "One ruling record for the rule" bullet, the rewritten Acceptance note, the findings-commit Verification block), the corrected changeset and the new ruling record each state the rule (what is judged on, what a refusal names, what answers not-found); none describes a probe or how a pre-fix door could be made to misbehave. No breach.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged: `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`, `Clause-②: no` with no arm, `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the body and both changesets. The delta publishes no code.
- **Should-fix (text) closed — every sentence of the corrected pending changeset is true of the tree.** Title: a refused write answers the same for a row it cannot read as for a missing one — true (the not-found for both). Lead sentence: the gate asks the administrator's own read whether the row is there to remove — true (`organizationTargets` → `callerRead`); the "now" overstates the delta from 18.3.0, which already read under the caller's context, a nit noted before and not a finding. Bullet 1, now scoped to a removal: the removal of an unreadable row answers as the removal of a missing id, the read door's `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` for that object and id — true (`unreadable` refusal → `recordNotFoundError`; an edit in place is refused before any lookup, so the scoping is right). Bullet 2: a readable row is judged on the stored row; a refusal names the organization boundary, and names the organization, position or permission set only when the administrator's own read returns that value as stored — true (`storedRow`, `mayName` on `organization_id`, `position`, `GRANT_SET_NAME_FIELD`; every organization-branch refusal is thrown with the "(ADR-0090 D12, the organization boundary)" tail). Bullet 3: an edit in place of a readable row is refused as before, every removal admitted before is still admitted, a tenant-level administrator is judged as before — true (the stored-row verdict admits a superset of the caller-read verdict; `isTenantLevelAdmin` returns before the branch). Read together with the new changeset `org-admin-removal-stored-row-verdict.md`, the two notes no longer contradict each other.
- `Check Changeset` will stay red on this head by the foreign-changeset rule, as designed; the maintainer's confirmation of this PR's correction is still the owed human step, now for the three corrected lines rather than one, and the body asks for it.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The changeset confirmation request** is restated in the body for the sentence and the two bullets; the Acceptance note's account of what each line now says matches the file byte for byte in substance. Owed to the maintainer; not this record's to give.
2. **The organization-column question** is now worded as "a separate change the seat has ordered". Consistent with the earlier record's reading (pre-existing, fail-closed, outside this PR's files); nothing in the delta touches it.
3. **Verification claims for the findings commits** (typecheck, 85/85, 157/157, the changeset gate reading only the declared correction, six text gates green) are not reproduced here. CI on this head at the time of this read: finished checks green (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Test UI`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs`, two Lint families); `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, the Dogfood Regression Gate, the remaining Lint families, `Live E2E UI`, the Test Core planner and the Type Check families still in progress. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; the Tier S landing waits on them.
4. **Head moved by findings-only commits**: the earlier record's ① to ④ on `d33de915d2` carry; this delta re-reads only what moved and finds no behaviour moved.
5. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; the `Implemented-by` branch and the adopting seat share a session id, and this delta was again run by an isolated subagent of that seat on the inputs the brief names.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits` file changed in behaviour, so ④ is the earlier record's, re-checked against the delta: the three docblock rewrites describe the code as it is (the stored read conditional on the caller's read; `reads` by strict equality; wording through `mayName`; the read-refusal and fault paths unchanged), and the new ruling record's four bullets are each implemented at the sites that now cite it. Nothing in the delta can change a verdict, a sentence or a read. No finding.

Findings: no must-fix; both earlier should-fixes closed; no new should-fix. Owed before a Tier S landing: the maintainer's written confirmation of this PR's changeset correction, the by-design-red comment on this PR for `Check Changeset`, and green on the gate-carrying checks still running on this head.
